precursor_signals: vibration amplitude climbing from 2.1mm/s to 9.8mm/s over 5 days
dominant frequency shift toward 1x rotational speed (bearing wear signature)
bearing housing temperature up from 58C to 74C
faint high-pitched whine reported by floor operators starting 2 days before failure
failure: Drive-end bearing seized, causing pump shaft misalignment and unplanned shutdown
repairs_attempted: Initial regreasing of bearing housing - did not reduce vibration, symptom persisted
final_fix: Replaced drive-end bearing (SKF 6309), realigned shaft to 0.05mm tolerance, replaced worn coupling
root_cause: Bearing lubrication interval had been extended from monthly to quarterly during a cost-cutting review 6 months prior, causing gradual grease starvation

precursor_signals: vibration amplitude climbing from 2.3mm/s to 8.9mm/s over 4 days
dominant frequency shift toward 1x rotational speed
bearing housing temperature up from 60C to 71C
same high-pitched whine reported by operators
failure: Drive-end bearing failure again, same location as MAINT-2025-001
final_fix: Replaced bearing, restored monthly lubrication schedule permanently, added vibration sensor alert threshold at 6mm/s
root_cause: Lubrication interval had quietly reverted to quarterly again after a maintenance software update reset the schedule template to its default

precursor_signals: discharge air temperature climbing from 85C to 118C over 3 hours
compressor cycling frequency increasing (short-cycling)
oil pressure gauge reading dropping slightly but within nominal range
failure: Compressor thermal overload trip, unit shut down automatically to prevent damage
repairs_attempted: Reset thermal trip and restarted - failed again within 20 minutes
final_fix: Cleaned severely fouled intercooler fins, replaced clogged air intake filter
root_cause: Intake filter had not been replaced on schedule due to a supply chain delay in filter stock, causing restricted airflow and heat buildup

precursor_signals: discharge air temperature climbing from 86C to 121C over 4 hours
compressor cycling frequency increasing
same pattern as MAINT-2025-003
failure: Thermal overload trip again on same unit
final_fix: Replaced intake filter immediately based on flagged historical pattern, avoided full inspection cycle
root_cause: Filter replacement schedule still relied on a fixed calendar interval rather than airflow-based triggering, so a filter nearing end-of-life again went unnoticed until temperature symptoms appeared

precursor_signals: spindle motor current draw increasing 15% above baseline under identical load
surface finish quality degrading on finished parts (visible chatter marks)
audible grinding noise during high-speed operation reported by operator
failure: Spindle bearing failure causing complete spindle seizure mid-cut, scrapping the workpiece
repairs_attempted: Reduced spindle speed to compensate for noise - masked symptom temporarily, did not resolve underlying wear
final_fix: Replaced spindle bearing cartridge assembly, recalibrated spindle runout to spec
root_cause: Coolant delivery nozzle had drifted out of alignment months earlier, causing insufficient cooling at the spindle bearing during extended high-speed runs

precursor_signals: spindle motor current draw increasing above baseline
surface finish quality degrading with chatter marks reappearing
same signature as MAINT-2025-005
failure: Early signs caught before full seizure - spindle bearing showed wear consistent with prior failure pattern
final_fix: Preemptively replaced spindle bearing during scheduled downtime, checked and corrected coolant nozzle alignment as part of the fix this time
root_cause: Coolant nozzle alignment check had never been added to the standard maintenance checklist after the first incident, so the same misalignment recurred unnoticed over months

precursor_signals: motor casing temperature climbing from 65C to 95C over 6 hours
belt tracking drifting slightly off-center
intermittent motor stall alarms beginning 30 minutes before full failure
failure: Motor winding insulation breakdown from sustained overheating, motor failed completely
repairs_attempted: Manually recentered belt tracking - temporarily reduced stall alarms but temperature continued climbing
final_fix: Replaced motor, corrected belt tension which was root cause of tracking drift and motor strain
root_cause: Belt tension had loosened gradually due to normal wear without a scheduled tension-check interval, causing the motor to work harder and overheat over weeks

precursor_signals: hydraulic system pressure fluctuating outside normal band during cycle
cycle time increasing gradually over 2 weeks
small hydraulic fluid stains observed near cylinder seals
failure: Cylinder seal failure caused sudden pressure loss mid-press, halting production and requiring fluid cleanup
final_fix: Replaced cylinder seals, flushed and replaced hydraulic fluid, inspected cylinder bore for scoring
root_cause: Hydraulic fluid had not been tested for contamination on schedule, and particulate contamination accelerated seal wear

precursor_signals: refrigerant pressure trending downward slowly over 10 days
compressor run time increasing to maintain setpoint temperature
condenser fan cycling more frequently than baseline
failure: Low refrigerant charge triggered compressor low-pressure safety cutoff, chiller stopped cooling
repairs_attempted: Topped off refrigerant without locating the leak - pressure dropped again within 3 weeks
final_fix: Located and repaired a slow leak at a brazed joint using UV dye trace, recharged system properly, retested for leaks
root_cause: A brazed joint had a micro-leak from initial installation that was never caught because prior refrigerant top-offs treated the symptom, not the leak itself

precursor_signals: joint 3 servo motor current draw showing irregular spikes during specific motion paths
positional accuracy drifting by small but increasing margins on repeated cycles
audible clicking sound from joint 3 gearbox during deceleration
failure: Joint 3 gearbox backlash became severe enough to cause weld placement errors, failing quality inspection on multiple parts
repairs_attempted: Recalibrated positional offsets in software - masked the drift temporarily but clicking sound and current spikes continued
final_fix: Replaced joint 3 gearbox assembly, verified backlash within spec, re-ran calibration
root_cause: Gearbox lubricant had degraded past service life without a condition-based replacement trigger, only a fixed calendar interval that hadn't yet elapsed

precursor_signals: motor casing temperature climbing gradually, same pattern as MAINT-2025-007
belt tracking drift detected early via new sensor alert
no stall alarms yet
failure: Caught before motor damage - belt tension found loose again during proactive inspection triggered by pattern match
final_fix: Retensioned belt during scheduled maintenance window, added belt tension to the standard weekly inspection checklist
root_cause: Belt tension check still wasn't part of any recurring schedule after the first incident five months earlier, only added now after this second occurrence
